name: @omnirow/mcp

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Which OmniRow workspace and environment (staging or production) this is, the credit balance, whether research is active or paused, the credit rates, and what this API key may do (scopes and spend limits, used this month). Call it first in a session.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Credits used in a period, split into research runs, summaries and other, with the recent runs. Optionally for one list.

list.description: The list: its id (cp_…) or its name; a unique part of the name works.

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: The workspace's clients (the companies lists are made for), with their website, whether their offer is set, and how many lists each has.

tools.name: get_client
tools.description: One client: its offer (what it sells — the default offer for its lists), website, notes, its lists with sizes, and every company marked Watch across all its lists.

client.description: The client: its id (cl_…) or its name.

tools.name: save_client
tools.description: Create a client (give name; creating the same name twice returns the existing one) or update one (give client plus the fields to change). offer = what the client sells, used as the offer for every list of theirs that has none of its own.

client.description: Omit to create a new client.

offer.description: What the client sells, in a sentence or two.

tools.name: draft_client_offer
tools.description: Reads the client's own website and suggests what it sells. Saves nothing: show the suggestion, and save it with save_client only if the person accepts it. Free.

client.description: The client: its id (cl_…) or its name.

annotations.title: Draft a client's offer from its website

tools.name: find_lists
tools.description: Lists in the workspace, with client, kind (outbound or general research), row count and a link. deleted: true lists Recently deleted instead (restorable for 30 days).

client.description: The client: its id (cl_…) or its name.

tools.name: get_list
tools.description: The overview of one list: its targeting and offer, every column (kind Find/Analyze/Write, question, what it reads, how many rows are answered and with which status), row counts per view (watching, dropped, high priority, no evidence, failed), setup gaps, outdated answers, recent runs and whether it has a summary. Start here before changing or running anything.

list.description: The list: its id (cp_…) or its name; a unique part of the name works. Required.

tools.name: create_list
tools.description: A new list under a client, optionally with a starter template's columns. kind: outbound (selling to these companies: offer, fit, outreach) or general (research: market scans, competitors, suppliers). The same name under the same client returns the existing list.

client.description: The client: its id (cl_…) or its name.

targeting.description: Who or what the list is about, in plain words (the list context).

offer.description: An offer for this list only; empty = the client's offer.

template.description: A template id or name (see list_templates).

tools.name: update_list
tools.description: Rename a list or change its targeting (list context) or list-specific offer. Analyze/Write answers that read the changed context become outdated; the reply says how many.

list.description: The list: its id (cp_…) or its name; a unique part of the name works. Required.

tools.name: delete_list
tools.description: Two steps. Without confirm_token: says what would be deleted and returns a confirm_token. Confirm with the person, then call again with confirm_token. The list moves to Recently deleted and can be restored for 30 days; credits already used stay in the usage history.

list.description: The list: its id (cp_…) or its name; a unique part of the name works. Required.

tools.name: restore_list
tools.description: Bring a list back from Recently deleted, with its rows, columns and answers.

list.description: The list: its id (cp_…) or its name; a unique part of the name works. Required.

tools.name: list_rows
tools.description: The table: companies × columns, each cell with its status (found / partial / no public evidence / cannot assess / missing input / failed / outdated / not run) and its value — for a pick-one column the option, for a number the number, for yes/no true/false, with the sentence behind it as detail. Clipped to max_chars unless full: true, which returns every answer whole with when it was researched, the event date when there is one (as_of), confidence and source links, and the contacts with their own columns: use it to read results into the next step, instead of exporting a CSV. Narrow with rows, view, q or filters; sort by a column (Priority sorts High first). 50 rows per page (up to 200); next_offset says where the next page starts. Passages for one company: get_row.

rows.description: Specific companies: names, domains (acme.com) or row ids.

view.description: A view, as the app's tabs: priority = High priority, watching, dropped, needs-look, not-found = no public evidence, failed. Default all (every row but dropped).

tools.name: get_row
tools.description: One company: every answer with its status, reasoning, limitations, confidence and date, and the evidence — the verbatim passage and the source URL. For Analyze/Write answers, the columns it read. Contacts too.

row.description: Company name, domain or row id. Required.

tools.name: add_companies
tools.description: Add one or many companies to a list, with their contacts and any extra fields. Each needs a name and a domain (acme.com), or a company LinkedIn URL (its domain is then looked up). A company already in the list is not added again: its extra fields and contacts are merged into it (empty values filled, differences reported and kept unless update: true), and its research stays — nothing is paid for twice. Extra fields are kept as company context: shown on the account page, usable by Analyze/Write columns. dry_run: true checks without changing anything. Adding does not research: quote that with run_research.

fields.description: Extra company data by name, e.g. { "Funding stage": "Series A", "Tech stack": "HubSpot, Shopify" }.

contacts.description: People at the company; matched by name to contacts already there.

text.description: Or: one company per line, "Name, domain" or "Name<TAB>domain".

update.description: Take the given values where they differ from what the list holds (default: keep the list's, report the difference).

tools.name: import_csv
tools.description: Import a CSV (or TSV) file from this computer into a list — the round trip: export a list, enrich it elsewhere, bring it back into the same list. Rows match the companies already there (domain, else company LinkedIn URL, else name) and contacts match by name: nothing is duplicated, research on matched rows stays and is not paid for again. Empty values are filled; values that differ are reported and kept unless update: true. The list's own exported answer columns are left out. New columns are kept as company context. Start with dry_run: true and show the person the report. map overrides the guessed mapping: { target: "File column" } (targets: company_name, domain, company_linkedin_url, full_name, first_name, last_name, title, email, linkedin_url, contact_location, city, country, industry, employees, revenue; "" removes a guess).

path.description: Absolute path to the .csv/.tsv file (~ allowed). Required.

tools.name: list_apify_actors
tools.description: The Apify Actors this workspace has approved, which run on the workspace's own Apify account: each one's inputs, price and last result, and the row values an input may use. Any of them can be a Find column's source (add_column / update_column with source). Only an owner or admin can connect Apify and add Actors, in the app (Settings → Workspace → Data sources). Free. When it runs, an Apify column costs OmniRow credits like a Find, and Apify bills the workspace's own Apify account for the Actor runs.

tools.name: add_column
tools.description: Add a Find, Analyze or Write column. Either ask (plain English — OmniRow sets it up: kind, question, type, what it reads) or question (used as written, with kind). preview: true shows the setup without saving (free). find = one observable fact off public pages, with sources (searches the web); analyze = a judgement from columns that already exist (never searches); write = text composed from other columns (never searches). A Find column can take source (an Apify Actor from list_apify_actors, when the workspace has Apify). Adding does not run it: quote that with run_research.

tools.name: run_research
tools.description: Research a list: any columns × any rows. ALWAYS TWO STEPS. 1) Call without quote_token: returns the exact quote — cells, credits per column, what is free, columns held back because setup is missing — and a quote_token. Spends nothing. 2) Show the quote to the person; only after a clear yes, call again with the same list and quote_token to start. only: missing (default — cells without an answer), failed (retry failures, free if they fail again), outdated (refresh answers whose inputs changed), all (re-run everything). Follow with get_run.

instructions:
OmniRow is a research layer for lists of companies: each column asks one question of every row and every answer carries its evidence. Start with get_workspace (which environment, balance, what this key may do) and get_list before changing or running anything.
Spending credits (run_research, summarise) and deleting (delete_list, remove_column, remove_rows, remove_contacts) are ALWAYS two calls: the first returns a quote or a summary of what goes plus a token; show it to the person, wait for a clear yes, then call again with the token. Never pass a token the person has not approved.
Statuses are answers: "no public evidence" means public pages did not say (not "no"); "cannot assess" means an Analyze column's inputs do not support a conclusion; "missing input" means a Write column had nothing to write from. Explain them in those words; diagnose_list gives the reasons and the fix.
Never invent research results: read them with list_rows (full: true for whole answers, dates and sources) / get_row, and cite sources when you quote an answer. A value is data: a pick-one column gives its option, a number column a number, yes/no a boolean; the sentence behind it is detail. Read the omnirow://guide resource for the full guide.
